newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down 40 bps to 12.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down 40 bps to 12.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate fell 40 basis points to 12.3 percent in moderate trade on Monday, dealers said.
They put the total daily settlements at 34.5 million kuna. More than 10 million kuna were left on the supply side at the end of trading.
Fresh loans accounted for 27 million kuna, mostly call money granted at a steady 10.5 percent rate.
One-week to one-month rates were steady, ranging between 12 and 15 percent
Insurers rolled over previous loans at 12 and 14 percent, while banks charged 11.5 percent for old one-week borrowings and 15 to 16 percent for one-month loans.
The Central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday weaker at 6.1944 against the dollar and 3.5756 against the German mark.
